units.name: savedRoundingMode
units.rationale: BG-SAVE-M keeps the caller's rounding mode so the operation can be retried in big-number mode after a capacity overflow.

units.name: savedPrecisionOrScale
units.rationale: BG-SAVE-P keeps the caller's precision/scale parameter for the big-number retry.

units.name: SavedOperands
units.rationale: BG-SAVE is scratch that preserves the original operands and parameters so a fast-path overflow can be redone by the big-number path.

units.name: entryGeneration
units.rationale: BG-V-GEN stamps a stored big number with the store generation so stale handles are detected.

units.name: entryLimb
units.rationale: BG-V-L holds the base-10^9 limbs of a stored big number.

units.name: entryLength
units.rationale: BG-V-LEN is the number of limbs in a stored big number.

units.name: entrySign
units.rationale: BG-V-SG is the sign (-1, 0, 1) of a stored big number.

units.name: BigNumberStore
units.rationale: BG-STORE keeps up to 2500 big results; callers get a handle of generation times 10^6 plus slot.

units.name: operandALimb
units.rationale: BX-A-L holds operand A's base-10^9 limbs, least significant first.

units.name: operandALength
units.rationale: BX-A-LEN is the number of limbs in big operand A.

units.name: operandASign
units.rationale: BX-A-SG is the sign (-1, 0, 1) of big operand A.

units.name: operandBLimb
units.rationale: BX-B-L holds operand B's base-10^9 limbs.

units.name: operandBLength
units.rationale: BX-B-LEN is the number of limbs in big operand B.

units.name: operandBSign
units.rationale: BX-B-SG is the sign of big operand B (negated for subtraction).

units.name: quotientLimb
units.rationale: BX-Q-L receives the quotient limbs of the big division.

units.name: quotientLength
units.rationale: BX-Q-LEN is the number of limbs in the quotient.

units.name: quotientSign
units.rationale: BX-Q-SG is the sign of the quotient register (set positive for the magnitude division).

units.name: resultLimb
units.rationale: BX-R-L holds the limbs of the big result.

units.name: resultLength
units.rationale: BX-R-LEN is the number of limbs in the big result.

units.name: resultSign
units.rationale: BX-R-SG is the sign of the big result.

units.name: remainderLimb
units.rationale: BX-T-L receives the remainder limbs of the magnitude division (also a swap register).

units.name: remainderLength
units.rationale: BX-T-LEN is the number of limbs in the division remainder.

units.name: remainderSign
units.rationale: BX-T-SG is the sign of the division remainder.

units.name: normalizedDividendLimb
units.rationale: BX-U holds the dividend multiplied by the normalisation factor in the long (Knuth) division.

units.name: normalizedDividendLength
units.rationale: BX-U-LEN is the limb count of the normalised dividend.

units.name: normalizedDividendSign
units.rationale: BX-U-SG is the sign of the normalised dividend register, cleared when it trims to zero.

units.name: normalizedDivisorLimb
units.rationale: BX-V holds the divisor multiplied by the normalisation factor in the long division.

units.name: normalizedDivisorLength
units.rationale: BX-V-LEN is the limb count of the normalised divisor.

evidence.quote: PERFORM VARYING BX-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL BX-I > BX-V-LEN

units.name: normalizedDivisorSign
units.rationale: BX-V-SG is the sign slot of the divisor register (copied with the divisor, not tested).

units.name: registerXLimb
units.rationale: BX-X is declared but never referenced; a spare big register with no role, so it is named structurally for review.

units.name: registerXLength
units.rationale: Limb count of the unused spare register BX-X.

units.name: registerXSign
units.rationale: Sign of the unused spare register BX-X.

units.name: registerYLimb
units.rationale: BX-Y is declared but never referenced; a spare big register named structurally for review.

units.name: registerYLength
units.rationale: Limb count of the unused spare register BX-Y.

units.name: registerYSign
units.rationale: Sign of the unused spare register BX-Y.

units.name: BigNumberRegisters
units.rationale: BX-REGS are the multi-limb (base 10^9) number registers of the big-number arithmetic: operands, result, quotient, remainder, normalised dividend and divisor.

units.name: unusedBs
units.rationale: BX-BS is declared but never referenced and nothing shows its meaning; flagged for removal or review.

units.name: borrow
units.rationale: BX-BW is the borrow carried between limbs in magnitude subtraction.

units.name: carry
units.rationale: BX-C is the carry between limbs in addition and multiplication.

units.name: magnitudeComparison
units.rationale: BX-CMP is the -1/0/1 result of comparing the magnitudes of A and B.

units.name: storeSlot
units.rationale: BX-E is the slot of a big number in the store, decoded from or encoded into a handle.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-H BY 1000000 GIVING BX-G REMAINDER BX-E

units.name: limbFactor
units.rationale: BX-F is a single-limb multiplier or divisor: a power of ten for shifts, the normalisation factor, or a one-limb divisor.

units.name: handleGeneration
units.rationale: BX-G is the generation decoded from a big-number handle, checked against the slot's generation.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-H BY 1000000 GIVING BX-G REMAINDER BX-E

units.name: handle
units.rationale: BX-H is a big-number handle (generation times 10^6 plus slot) passed in place of an unscaled value.

units.name: index
units.rationale: BX-I is the main limb loop index.

evidence.quote: PERFORM VARYING BX-I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL BX-I > BX-N

units.name: combinedIndex
units.rationale: BX-IJ is the summed index i + j into the product or dividend limbs.

units.name: secondIndex
units.rationale: BX-J is the inner (operand B / quotient position) loop index.

evidence.quote: PERFORM VARYING BX-J FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL BX-J >

units.name: dividendTopIndex
units.rationale: BX-J1 = j + n + 1 indexes the top dividend limb used to estimate a quotient digit.

units.name: dividendNextIndex
units.rationale: BX-J2 = j + n indexes the next dividend limb for the quotient estimate.

units.name: dividendThirdIndex
units.rationale: BX-J3 = j + n - 1 indexes the third dividend limb used to correct the estimate.

units.name: shiftDigits
units.rationale: BX-K is the number of decimal digits a big number is shifted (multiplied by 10^k) to align scales.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-K BY 9 GIVING BX-KL REMAINDER BX-KD

units.name: secondShiftDigits
units.rationale: BX-K2 is declared but never referenced; named after its apparent twin BX-K for review.

units.name: shiftRemainderDigits
units.rationale: BX-KD is the part of the shift below one limb (k mod 9 digits), applied by a power-of-ten multiply.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-K BY 9 GIVING BX-KL REMAINDER BX-KD

units.name: shiftLimbs
units.rationale: BX-KL is the whole-limb part of the shift (k div 9), applied by moving limbs up.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-K BY 9 GIVING BX-KL REMAINDER BX-KD

units.name: lengthDifference
units.rationale: BX-M is the dividend length minus the divisor length, which sizes the quotient.

units.name: limbCount
units.rationale: BX-N is a working limb count (product length, longer operand, divisor length).

units.name: twoLimbNumerator
units.rationale: BX-NUM joins the top two dividend limbs to estimate the next quotient digit.

units.name: quotientParity
units.rationale: BX-ODD is the parity of the quotient's lowest limb, used for half-even rounding.

units.name: limbProduct
units.rationale: BX-P holds a limb product or sum including carry before it is split into limb and carry.

units.name: productLowLimb
units.rationale: BX-PL is the low limb of a quotient-digit times divisor-limb product.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-P BY 1000000000 GIVING BX-C REMAINDER BX-PL

units.name: limbPowerOfTen
units.rationale: BX-POW9 is the table 10^0 to 10^9 used for within-limb shifts and digit counts.

units.name: quotientEstimate
units.rationale: BX-QH is the estimated quotient digit (q-hat) of long division, corrected downward when too big.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-NUM BY BX-VT GIVING BX-QH REMAINDER BX-RH

units.name: quotientSign
units.rationale: BX-QS is the sign of the division result (sign of A times sign of B), applied after the magnitude division.

units.name: remainderEstimate
units.rationale: BX-RH is the remainder (r-hat) that goes with the quotient-digit estimate.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE BX-NUM BY BX-VT GIVING BX-QH REMAINDER BX-RH

units.name: operandAScale
units.rationale: BX-SA is operand A's scale during alignment.

units.name: operandBScale
units.rationale: BX-SB is operand B's scale during alignment.

units.name: resultScale
units.rationale: BX-SC is the scale of the big result returned in JB-R-S.

units.name: firstTemporary
units.rationale: BX-T1 is a general temporary (divisor top plus one, product, borrow-adjusted limb).

units.name: secondTemporary
units.rationale: BX-T2 is the second temporary of the quotient-digit correction test.

units.name: packedValue
units.rationale: BX-U31 is the 31-digit packed value converted to or from limbs.

units.name: divisorTopLimb
units.rationale: BX-VT is the most significant limb of the normalised divisor.

units.name: divisorSecondLimb
units.rationale: BX-VT2 is the second most significant limb of the normalised divisor.

units.name: packedQuotient
units.rationale: BX-W31 receives the packed value divided by 10^9 while it is split into limbs.

units.name: BigNumberScratch
units.rationale: BX-WORK is scratch for the big-number algorithms (indexes, carries, estimates); not a business entity.

units.name: absoluteAccumulator
units.rationale: W-A is the absolute value of the accumulator W-X, used to count its digits.

units.name: absoluteSecondOperand
units.rationale: W-B is never referenced; same picture as W-A, so presumably the absolute value of W-Y. Review.

units.name: largerScale
units.rationale: W-BIGS is never referenced; read as 'bigger scale' only from its letters. Review.

units.name: comparison
units.rationale: W-CMP is the -1/0/1 result of comparing the aligned values.

evidence.quote: WHEN W-X > W-Y MOVE 1 TO W-CMP

units.name: doubleValue
units.rationale: W-D is never referenced; it mirrors JB-D's picture, presumably for an unimplemented double conversion. Review.

units.name: operandADigits
units.rationale: W-DA is the digit count of operand A used to left-align it for comparison.

units.name: operandBDigits
units.rationale: W-DB is the digit count of operand B used to left-align it for comparison.

units.name: doubleUnscaled
units.rationale: W-DU redefines W-D as an integer (unscaled) view; never referenced. Review.

evidence.quote: 05 W-DU REDEFINES W-D PIC S9(18) COMP-3.

units.name: operandAUpscale
units.rationale: W-EA is the number of powers of ten the dividend is multiplied by before dividing.

units.name: operandBUpscale
units.rationale: W-EB is the number of powers of ten the divisor is multiplied by before dividing.

units.name: operandAAdjustedExponent
units.rationale: W-EST is A's digits plus exponent minus scale, the order of magnitude compared first.

units.name: hash
units.rationale: W-H is never referenced; it belongs to an H-group that presumably served the unimplemented HC (hash code) operation. Review.

units.name: operandBAdjustedExponent
units.rationale: W-HIGH is B's digits plus exponent minus scale, compared with A's.

units.name: hashLow
units.rationale: W-HL is never referenced; part of the presumed hash-code group. Review.

units.name: hashMultiplier
units.rationale: W-HM is never referenced; part of the presumed hash-code group. Review.

units.name: hashQuotient
units.rationale: W-HQ is never referenced; part of the presumed hash-code group. Review.

units.name: hashSecondQuotient
units.rationale: W-HQ2 is never referenced; part of the presumed hash-code group. Review.

units.name: hashRemainder
units.rationale: W-HR is never referenced; part of the presumed hash-code group. Review.

units.name: index
units.rationale: W-I is the loop index over the powers-of-ten table and digit counts.

evidence.quote: PERFORM VARYING W-I FROM 2 BY 1 UNTIL W-I > 31

units.name: roundIncrement
units.rationale: W-INC is never referenced; its twin BX-INC is the round-up flag of the big path. Review.

units.name: shiftDigits
units.rationale: W-K is the number of decimal digits to drop or to upscale by.

units.name: roundingMode
units.rationale: W-MODE is the rounding mode of the operation, translated from the JB-M code into letters.

units.name: ResolvedRoundingMode
units.rationale: Enum of the letter codes W-MODE resolves JB-M into; it adds UNNECESSARY, so it is kept distinct from the rounding kernel's RoundingMode.
JB-M codes 0 to 6 map to U, D, C, F, H, N, E (the BigDecimal rounding-mode order); anything else becomes X, which raises an ArithmeticException when digits would be lost, i.e. UNNECESSARY.

units.name: trailingZeros
units.rationale: W-N counts the trailing zeros stripped from a value by the ZEROS paragraph.

units.name: newScale
units.rationale: W-NEWS is the dividend precision minus the requested precision, the scale the divisor is adjusted towards.

units.name: accumulatorDigits
units.rationale: W-NX is the number of decimal digits in the accumulator W-X.

units.name: secondOperandDigits
units.rationale: W-NY is never referenced; twin of W-NX for W-Y. Review.

units.name: precision
units.rationale: W-P is never referenced; 'precision' is a guess from the letter and JB-P. Review.

units.name: preferredScale
units.rationale: W-PS is the division's preferred scale (dividend scale minus divisor scale); trailing zeros are stripped down to it.

evidence.quote: PERFORM UNTIL W-X = 0 OR W-S NOT > W-PS

units.name: quotient
units.rationale: W-Q is the quotient of the packed division.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE W-X BY W-Y GIVING W-Q REMAINDER W-R

units.name: remainder
units.rationale: W-R is the remainder of the packed division, which decides the rounding.

evidence.quote: DIVIDE W-X BY W-Y GIVING W-Q REMAINDER W-R

units.name: dividendRaise
units.rationale: W-RAISE is how many digits the dividend must be raised to give the requested precision.

units.name: resultExponent
units.rationale: W-RZ is the result's exponent (extra trailing zeros) returned in JB-R-Z.

units.name: resultScale
units.rationale: W-S is the scale of the value being built, returned in JB-R-S.

units.name: operandAScale
units.rationale: W-SA is A's scale when aligning, but is reused for A's precision in division and A's sign in compare; named for its first role.

units.name: operandBScale
units.rationale: W-SB is B's scale when aligning, reused for B's sign in compare.

units.name: quotientScale
units.rationale: W-SCL is the scale the quotient of divide-with-context gets before final rounding.

evidence.quote: COMPUTE W-SCL = W-PS + W-YS - W-SA + JB-P

units.name: sign
units.rationale: W-SG is never referenced; 'sign' is read from the letters only. Review.

units.name: smallerScale
units.rationale: W-SMS is never referenced; read as 'smaller scale', twin of W-BIGS. Review.
W-STICKY is the rounding sticky flag: Y when a non-zero remainder lies beyond the retained digit; passed on to the rounding kernel.

units.name: temporary
units.rationale: W-T is a general temporary: swap holder, extra quotient digit, rounding increment.

units.name: savedValue
units.rationale: W-U parks a value while W-X is reused (stripped dividend, |A|, a remainder for the sticky test).

units.name: hashWord
units.rationale: W-W (4 occurrences) is never referenced; presumed part of the hash-code group. Review.

units.name: accumulator
units.rationale: W-X is the working unscaled value every fast-path operation builds and returns in JB-R-U.

units.name: secondOperand
units.rationale: W-Y holds the second (aligned) operand or divisor.

units.name: divisorPrecision
units.rationale: W-YS is the divisor's digit count plus exponent, i.e. its precision, in divide-with-context.

units.name: operandAExponent
units.rationale: W-ZA is the working copy of operand A's exponent (JB-A-Z).

units.name: operandBExponent
units.rationale: W-ZB is the working copy of operand B's exponent (JB-B-Z).

units.name: PackedDecimalScratch
units.rationale: W-AREA is the scratch of the 31-digit packed (fast) arithmetic path; an algorithm area, not an entity.

units.name: powerOfTen
units.rationale: W-POW(i) holds 10 to the power i-1.

units.name: DecimalPowerTable
units.rationale: W-POWERS is the decimal kernel's powers-of-ten table, distinct from the rounding kernel's.

notes.text: A numeric rounding-mode code 0..6 that maps to UP, DOWN, CEILING, FLOOR, HALF_UP, HALF_DOWN, HALF_EVEN is Java RoundingMode order; the catch-all that throws when digits would be lost is UNNECESSARY.

Library scratch areas carry fields that are never referenced (spare registers, groups for unimplemented op codes); check references before naming and send such fields to review rather than inventing roles.
